thread:
Ana: Hey leadership Q&A notes — summarizing the pricing/quotas parts so we can post a clean followup. Please correct any inaccuracies.

Mira: Two quick things — are rate-limits per-API-key or per-organization? Also, do retries count against burst windows?

Sam: Rate limits are per-API-key. We also apply organization-level protective caps to avoid runaway bills; those are softer (alerts + temporary throttles). Retries do consume tokens and count toward burst, so exponential backoff is recommended.

Mira: Thanks. For streaming endpoints, is the billing model different? We see long streams hammering throughput.

Sam: Streaming is metered by active token generation QPS and counts against the same throughput quota. Long-lived streams will use capacity while open; short lived ones are fine.

Julia: What happens when credits hit zero? Any grace behavior or failover for critical jobs?

FinanceBot: Accounts without auto-topup enter a 7-day grace period after balance zero. During grace, non-critical requests are deprioritized; admin/console operations remain. After seven days, non-admin calls are suspended.

Kevin: Dedicated customers have reserved throughput and are exempt from hosted soft caps. Private deployments control their own limits via config.

Ana: Can support temporarily raise quotas for production incidents? What's the typical SLA for emergency increases?

Kevin: Yes — support can provision emergency quota raises for verified P0s. Submit a support ticket with the incident link. Target response is 1-2 hours for urgent raises; larger sustained allotments take longer.

Sam: Feature FYI for eng: /v1/account/limits will return effective per-key throughput and remaining burst window. We'll add docs and an SDK helper soon.

Julia: Embeddings — are they charged differently and can they trigger separate throttles?

FinanceBot: Embeddings are billed per-vector units and sized accordingly. For throttling we map embedding requests to quota-equivalent units so heavy embedding workloads can be limited separately from text generation.

Mira: Any recommended best practices for customers to avoid unexpected throttles?

Sam: Use separate keys for CI, avoid sharing keys across many services, add backoff/retry, warm caches, and consider reserved capacity if you need predictable throughput.

Ana: OK I'll turn this into a short FAQ and link to it here. Sam/Finance/Kevin please review before we publish.

Sam: Will do — I'll post a short technical note in #eng and open a docs PR tonight. :thumbsup:

Ana: Thanks everyone — dropping the draft later today. If you have specific examples (logs, request patterns) paste them here.
